كَارِبٌ [Becoming near; drawing near; approaching]: near; nigh. (TA.) ―
-b2- 'Abd-Keys Ibn-Khufáf El-Burjumee says, “أَبُنَىَّ إِنَّ أَبَاكَ كَارِبُ يَوْمِهِ
فَإِذَا دُعِيتَ إِلَى المَكَارِمِ فَٱعْجَلِ
” [O my child, verily thy father is near to his day (of death): therefore when thou shalt be called to (the performance of ) generous actions, make haste]. (S.) ＝
-A2- أَمْرٌ كَارِبُ An afflicting, distressing, or oppressive, affair. (TA.)
From An Arabic-English Lexicon (Edward William Lane)
